dossier.public_summary: The dip recurs on the target star but shows a second, deep eclipse at half an orbit and large out-of-eclipse brightness swings, both as strong as the dip itself. The eclipse depth changes by a factor of two between sectors and the duration is too long for the small star. Together this is a close stellar grazing binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: A secondary eclipse at half phase with ~32% of the primary depth is too deep for a planet and matches a grazing/hot stellar binary. Sector_sec_half_max_snr 10.52 and sector_sec_half_sectors_over_3 2 shows it persists.
reasons.value: snr 8.6 at phase 0.4941, depth 2051 ppm, depth_over_dip 0.3178, snr_at_half 8.391

reasons.why: Out-of-eclipse variation as large as the transit indicates ellipsoidal/spot modulation from a close binary, not a planet.
Depth changes by ~2.4x within the same pipeline; an on-target planet should be steady, this favors blended/stellar dilution or ellipsoidal change not calibration.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source, TESS-SPOC p_constant 1.217332598146407e-06, depths 8850 ppm (S1), 6073 ppm (S28), 3741 ppm (S68), 7557 ppm (S92) depth_change_pct 77.94

reasons.why: Centroid rules out a neighbour eclipse (could_cause_within_1px 0, plausible_within_1px 0), so the binary must be on the target.
reasons.value: verdict on_target offset 1.533 arcsec err 1.691 sigma 0.9067

reasons.why: Flat bottom and long duration prove a near-central, grazing stellar eclipse with density mismatch, not a planetary transit.
Independent classifier rates this as planet-like only 9% of the time, consistent with other false-positive signatures.
